title: Policy engine: route-level experiment evaluator (deterministic bucketing + precedence)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Implement policy evaluation changes to apply experiments at the route/request-routing layer. Evaluator must (a) deterministically assign requests to experiment variants using the stickiness key strategy from ADR-047, (b) enforce precedence rules when a route has multiple policies (canary rollout, fallbacks, region routing), and (c) plumb attribution into the routing decision output so downstream request context/telemetry can tag {route, experiment_id, variant_id}.

Context
Console will create/activate route experiments (A/B/n) in the control plane (ENG-9021, ENG-9024). Router/policy engine must evaluate experiments consistently across regions and restarts.

Key requirements
1) Deterministic assignment / bucketing
- Same stickiness input must always map to same variant for a given {experiment_id, config_version}.
- Assignment must be stable across regions and service restarts.
- Must support explicit customer-provided stickiness key, plus safe fallbacks when missing.
- Must support N variants with arbitrary allocation weights (validated upstream, but evaluator must handle edge cases defensively).

2) Precedence rules
- Experiments are defined at the route level; evaluator runs as part of route policy evaluation.
- Define unambiguous ordering vs existing rollout policies:
  - Route match -> experiment eligibility -> experiment variant selection -> then apply canary/fallback policies within the chosen variant’s target (or apply canary only when experiment is not active; see decision below).
  - Fallback policy must not override experiment selection unless the chosen variant target is unhealthy/unavailable.
  - When both canary rollout and experiment are configured for the same route, experiments take precedence for selection; canary is treated as “inside” the variant’s target if applicable (i.e., variant points at a rollout target rather than raw model).

3) Eligibility + guardrails hooks
- Eligibility rules from config (e.g., header predicates, customer tier, region allowlist) must be evaluated before bucketing.
- If request is ineligible or missing required identifiers, evaluator must default to control (or “no experiment”) based on config semantics.
- Evaluator must emit decision metadata for debugging (hash inputs, selected bucket, config_version).

4) Performance / safety
- Added evaluation must be low overhead (<1ms p99 in policy evaluation benchmark) and allocation-free in hot paths.
- Safe defaults: if experiment config is unavailable/stale (handled more in ENG-9023), evaluator must fail open to baseline routing (no experiment) and set a reason code.

Decision summary (from architecture + cross-team threads)
- Hash inputs: HMAC-SHA256(key=service_secret, msg=experiment_id + config_version + stickiness_key) then take first 64 bits for bucket.
- Bucket -> variant: compute cumulative weight ranges over [0, 1). Use integer math over 10,000 basis points to avoid float drift.
- Stickiness key precedence (highest to lowest):
  1) Explicit request header "x-rw-experiment-sticky" (customer-provided stable id)
  2) Redwood customer_id (account) if present
  3) API key id (not raw key) if present
  4) (Last resort) request_id — permitted only when config allows non-sticky sampling; otherwise mark “ineligible_missing_sticky” and route to control
- Precedence: experiment selection happens before fallback evaluation. Fallback may activate only if chosen target errors/unhealthy/unavailable.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] For a fixed {experiment_id, config_version, sticky_key}, routing decision always returns the same variant_id across regions.
- [x] Allocation accuracy: simulated traffic over 1M synthetic keys matches configured weights within ±0.5% absolute for each variant (with deterministic seed).
- [x] Missing sticky key behavior matches config: default-to-control when required; optional non-sticky sampling only when explicitly enabled.
- [x] Route with both canary and experiment: experiment decides first; canary does not “steal” traffic outside variant selection.
- [x] Router fallback does not override variant selection unless selected target fails health check; emits reason code "fallback_after_variant_failure".
- [x] Emits decision debug fields in policy evaluation output (not necessarily customer-visible): experiment_id, variant_id, config_version, sticky_source, decision_reason.
- [x] Unit tests cover: weight boundaries, N>2 variants, zero-weight variant rejection (defensive), cross-version changes, eligibility filtering.

Implementation notes
- New evaluator module: ExperimentEvaluator.evaluate(route_ctx, request_ctx, policy_state) -> ExperimentDecision
- Decision includes:
  - experiment_applied: bool
  - experiment_id / variant_id / config_version
  - sticky_source: header|customer_id|api_key|request_id|none
  - reason: eligible|ineligible|missing_sticky|config_unavailable|variant_zero_weight|hash_error
- Weight mapping uses bps_sum; if sum != 10,000 treat as invalid config and fail open (also log + metric).
- Metrics (low-cardinality) to be emitted by policy engine:
  - experiment_eval_total{route_id, decision_reason}
  - experiment_eval_latency_ms (histogram)
  - experiment_eval_config_invalid_total

Links
- Confluence ADR-047 Deterministic Experiment Bucketing
- Confluence ADR-048 Experiment Metrics Attribution Schema
- PRs: pr-28433-policy-engine-experiment-bucketing-evaluator, pr-28457-router-apply-route-experiment-before-fallback

Risks / open questions (captured for beta)
- Cardinality: do not tag high-cardinality sticky_source/sticky_key into metrics; debug endpoint should be internal-only.
- Overlapping experiments on the same route: evaluator assumes control plane validation blocks this for GA; if overlap occurs, apply highest-priority experiment only and emit "overlap_detected" reason.

Rollout plan
- Ship behind feature flag route_experiments_enabled (allowlist accounts/regions).
- Stage in staging with synthetic traffic; verify split distribution and determinism across restarts.
- Enable for beta design partners after ENG-9023 (config propagation) lands.
comments: 2025-02-04 (Jordan Lee): Drafted evaluator API + decision struct. Starting with integer bps allocation to avoid float drift. Will align hash inputs with ADR-047 once final wording lands.

2025-02-06 (Jada Williams): Please ensure precedence is explicit when both canary and experiment exist. We’ve seen confusion where fallback ran first and masked the experiment. Suggest ordering: experiment -> target -> fallback-on-failure only.
2025-02-10 (Allison Grant): For metrics, keep tags minimal. We should rely on OTel span attributes for high-cardinality debug. Add a single counter by decision_reason and histogram for eval latency.
2025-02-12 (Ethan Park): +1 on failing open to baseline when config missing/stale. ENG-9023 will define staleness bounds; evaluator should just return reason codes and not block routing.

2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Add explicit reason code when fallback triggers after variant selection. This is crucial for the on-call runbook to separate “experiment changed behavior” from “backend instability”.

2025-02-24 (Jordan Lee): Implemented HMAC-based hash with service secret. Added stickiness key precedence order (header > customer_id > api_key_id). Missing sticky key currently defaults to request_id; will change to control unless config allows non-sticky sampling (per ADR feedback).

2025-02-26 (Marissa Cole): Product requirement: customers must be able to force stickiness via SDK/header; please ensure deterministic assignment even if they include extra whitespace/casing differences. Normalization needed.
2025-02-27 (Jordan Lee): Added normalization: trim + UTF-8 encode; reject empty string as missing. Added unit tests for boundary buckets (0, 9999, 10000).
2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): Please add micro-benchmark numbers to the ticket before closing. Goal <1ms p99 per evaluation in policy engine. Also ensure logs don’t include sticky key raw values.

2025-03-05 (Jordan Lee): Bench results (staging, 99th): evaluator 0.43ms p99, 0.12ms p50 with config in-memory; no allocs in hot path. Logs redact sticky key; debug fields only in internal explain endpoint output.
2025-03-12 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed decision object includes experiment_id/variant_id/config_version so Console request context plumbing (ENG-9026 / PR-28470) can attach to spans/metrics.
2025-03-21 (Ethan Park): Marking Done. Follow-up: ensure control plane blocks overlapping experiments by GA; evaluator’s overlap handling is best-effort only.
